integration_type: Existing assistant runtime interruption lifecycle, not a new provider integration

defaults.compatibility: Preserve legacy option lookup, transcript behavior, greeting policy and EOS delivery

flow: Adapter selects policy and changes message lifecycle
Control and output work proceed through independently scheduled handlers
Model, TTS and channel own separate resources and stopping boundaries
Generated assistant text and synthesis completion do not prove receiver playback

evidence.finding: The packet contract labels VAD and word evidence as an already detected interruption, coupling observation to policy
VAD speech start and end directly emit InterruptionDetectedPacket instead of neutral activity evidence
A nonblank transcript can rotate context immediately; there is no overlap-scoped hold/release gate
AssistantSpeaking is set when TTS audio is forwarded, not from a local sink playout receipt
Unconditional rotation is individually locked but separate caller reads do not form a conditional atomic transition
Repeated turn-rotation paths enqueue activation and interruption independently
Asynchronous packets run independently; lane order is not completion order
Interruption leaves currentPacket active; completion can append history before adapter-level rejection
Mutable current context and connection ownership need targeted cancellation review
evidence.verification: static interleaving analysis, not an executed race reproduction

evidence.finding: Destructive buffer clearing has no response argument or reversible pause acknowledgment
Byte buffer is not a response-aware playback ledger
Provider work uses conversation stream context; current protocol does not expose per-request cancellation

limitations: No new regression probe was written or executed
No live provider or audio trial was performed
No claim of exact receiver playback position
No upstream request cancellation through local invalidation
No independent approval of this design
